open.title: Reduce native canonical scan counter writes
open.head: d147a60fc4845e898d98d8924968d6094b417007
open.body:
## Problem

The native canonical-content scanner declares all seven header words volatile, so ordinary row counters repeatedly read and write memory inside the scan. Only journal progress must be visible before each authoritative mutation for synchronous rollback after a trap.

## Change

Accumulate the cursor, pending, exact, resolved and dense counts in local variables. Publish them at every normal return, negative return, exact-batch boundary and intentional fault-test trap. Keep journal progress volatile and retain its existing publication-before-mutation compiler barrier.

The native ABI, scratch layout, journal width, validation and persistent data formats are unchanged. The pinned Clang/LLD 21.1.8 kernel was regenerated; its module grows from 1,624 to 1,760 bytes.

## Validation

- 59 focused tests passed. The new direct native comparisons cover all seven header words, complete output/journal/exact descriptors and authoritative arena bytes on success, errors, continuations and first/middle/late traps.
- The existing owner suite now includes an AbortError exact-read rollback/retry case among 64 differential controls.
- All 219 locked Jitendex banks / 436,555 rows passed captured native-state parity across 55 component calls, including 363,243 pending rows and 38 exact hits, without a fallback group.
- Scoped lint, test TypeScript and pinned native reproduction passed.
- A retained 12-round local component comparison is inconclusive: candidate/control changes overlap the unchanged-product drift. It is not a complete-import speed result.
- Full units, builds, PR CI and isolated complete-browser comparisons are in progress. This remains a draft; no whole-import or process-memory improvement is claimed.

Baseline: `d24b4e56ceb1fe14ad96ef3853f4d397efa6fa26`. Candidate: `d147a60fc4845e898d98d8924968d6094b417007`. Source tree: `e3b9546229ac4118cc3e539678522446d74cff1d`.

Original changes to the repository's existing GPL-covered implementation. The small baseline test module is the exact source-bound artifact from the baseline commit, used solely as the partial-state oracle. No third-party implementation code was added. This does not include the separate compact-journal proposal.

open.title: Reduce media requirement allocation during dictionary imports
open.head: ebb0777114578c5cee879877274e7d872bfea27e
open.body:
## Problem

Projected dictionary images already own the diagnostic key bytes needed for errors, but import bookkeeping wraps those bytes in an entry object and clones the requirement again when deferring media. Dense ZIP setup also allocates a temporary assignment object per entry, and packed media copies and sorts its records even when they are already in physical archive order.

## Change

- Create one internal projected media requirement containing its path and owned diagnostic fields, and reuse it through deferred resolution.
- Attach the shared data reader directly to each private dense ZIP entry.
- Detect nondecreasing physical offsets during the existing validation pass. Reuse that record order when possible, retaining the sorted-copy fallback for other request orders.

The existing diagnostic-byte copy boundary, first-reference ordering, ordinary image target/getter behavior, cancellation, CRC checks, header/range validation and persistence format are preserved.

## Validation

- 140 focused tests passed, including immediate and deferred resolution, copied diagnostic keys after parser memory reuse, mixed projected/fallback references, first-reference errors, sorted/reversed/duplicate ZIP offsets, and cancellation joining an active read.
- Main/test TypeScript, scoped ESLint and the all-target build dry run passed.
- Independent review of this frozen change found no blocker.
- Full units, locked-corpus media parity, PR CI and frozen browser comparisons are in progress. This is a draft; no complete-import speedup or browser memory reduction is claimed yet.

Baseline: `d24b4e56ceb1fe14ad96ef3853f4d397efa6fa26`. Candidate: `ebb0777114578c5cee879877274e7d872bfea27e`. Source tree: `923cd36b875afbbee6e6674fd1b4450bed6ce362`.

Original changes to the repository's existing GPL-covered implementation; no third-party implementation code was added. This follows the existing projected-diagnostics path and is separate from the numeric media-path and direct media-entry proposals.

open.title: Skip sequence interning hashes for ordered import IDs
open.head: ec4e81395a1eb0f6f5fbf4f6d4c591201887e8cf
open.body:
## Problem

The native lookup-index encoder hashes and inserts every distinct sequence ID even when the source IDs are already increasing. JMdict and Jitendex contain long ordered runs, while VNDB repeatedly uses one ID.

## Change

Append first-seen increasing IDs directly to the existing sequence-key array. Repeated IDs keep the existing adjacent-value shortcut, including across absent sequences. On the first decrease, clear and backfill the existing hash table once, then use the original probing algorithm for the remaining rows.

First-seen key order, validation, error returns, persisted index bytes, scratch allocation and the native ABI are preserved. The pinned Clang/LLD 21.1.8 parser module was regenerated with its source-bound manifest; the module grows from 62,783 to 63,004 bytes.

## Validation

- 107 focused tests passed, covering independent JavaScript encoder parity, collisions, late decreases, maximum supported cardinality, negative gaps, dirty scratch reuse, error recovery and output guards.
- All 7,613,164 rows across 937 locked JMdict, Jitendex and VNDB banks passed the complete component oracle: native parser columns, keys, numeric fields, content, lookup-index bytes and media projections match the baseline, with independent source JSON and ZIP checks.
- That corpus oracle uses declared sequential four-bank component groups. It excludes worker transport, compression and persistence, and its work counts are not browser-planner counts.
- Scoped lint, test TypeScript, pinned native reproduction and the all-target build dry run passed.
- Full unit/PR CI and frozen complete-browser comparisons are in progress. This remains a draft pending those results; no complete-import speedup is claimed yet.

Baseline: `d24b4e56ceb1fe14ad96ef3853f4d397efa6fa26`. Candidate: `ec4e81395a1eb0f6f5fbf4f6d4c591201887e8cf`. Source tree: `3dd10f7c9b24e9ba3429a4d65540210a86d17fa3`.

open.title: perf: fuse UTF-8 continuation validation and copying
open.head: cb9f241106ab1529fa21c112f1733849c188511c
open.body:
## Problem

New unescaped multibyte keys validate their UTF-8 continuation bytes, then traverse those same bytes again to copy them into the native string arena. This path is used by the production fused parser as well as the separate native interner.

## Change

Validate and copy each continuation byte in one loop. Preserve the existing width, overlong-encoding, surrogate, truncation and fallback checks. Failed partial copies remain in the unpublished arena tail.

The production change is three added lines and two removed lines. Regenerate the WASM module and manifest with pinned LLVM/LLD 21.1.8; the module shrinks from 62,783 to 62,723 bytes while preserving the helper/inlining structure and fused-parser dispatch.

## Correctness validation

- All **7,613,164 rows across 937 banks** pass the frozen parent/candidate oracle: JMdict 528,299 rows, Jitendex 436,555, VNDB 6,648,310.
- Every source bank is independently inflated and CRC/size checked. Row keys/numeric fields and canonical content are checked against JSON; complete content, hash, lookup and media projections match the parent.
- 120 focused tests passed, including valid UTF-8 boundaries, malformed/truncated bytes, repeated keys and exact persisted lookup/content/hash equality through fused, separate-native and JavaScript paths.
- Pinned WASM rebuild check, all-target dry build and final main/test TypeScript checks passed.
- Source and both failure-handling callers independently reviewed.
- Published tree `655df9e9bd46fdd987a30473f2c3930007ce4e00` exactly matches tested local commit `d06c82c258de76b7ec6229397e4b85611dc592f4`.

The first full local unit run passed 14,386 tests but did not finish cleanly: two native-compiler setup errors and Android helper timeouts were retained. The compiler suites passed after correcting the local compiler wrapper. The unchanged parent Android suite and final isolated candidate rerun each passed 22/22 without changing the default five-second timeout or assertions. This does not make the earlier local full-suite invocation a pass. The final hosted full unit suite has now passed, and those original failures remain preserved.

## Performance limits

A fixed six-block Node 22 key-component screen had inconsistent small changes and large outliers. No end-to-end latency improvement is claimed. A broader UTF-8 specialization was rejected after control regressions; it is excluded from this PR.

[Full CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45266339914) has now passed all 15 active jobs; four conditional jobs were skipped. This includes the full unit suite, pinned WASM reproduction/build, all type/lint checks and Chromium/Firefox extension tests.

Their small timing differences do not establish a reliable speed improvement. The [VNDB cohort](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45266391385) is still running.

## Evidence

open.title: perf: compact native import rollback journals
open.head: 8282d596809d76ca2960f926719d94877925489e
open.body:
## Summary

The native canonical scanner writes rollback metadata for every newly inserted term-content identity. It currently records three uint32 values even though two are implied by the insertion invariants.

Store only the varying slot. JavaScript reconstructs the previous slot value as zero and the dense ID as `beforeDense + journalIndex`. This removes two stores and eight written bytes per native insertion for JMdict, Jitendex, and eligible VNDB segments.

The volatile progress publication and compiler barrier remain before authoritative mutation. The private ABI advances to 2, with matching source/module/build/release references and an actual ABI 1 fixture verifying safe fallback. Scratch reservation and persistent formats stay unchanged.

## Evidence

Compared against `develop` at `3d65e403c644b9a5a6be3128d72f9d30050b70e0` using the locked archives:

| Dictionary | Source rows checked | Native journal insertions | Written bytes avoided |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict | 528,299 | 354,890 | 2,839,120 |
| Jitendex | 436,555 | 363,243 | 2,905,944 |
| VNDB | 6,648,310 | 132,185 | 1,057,480 |

The complete native replay covers 937 banks and 209 native segments, using fixed four-bank component groups. Fallback rows are checked and excluded from native savings. A separate proof runs the actual baseline and candidate JavaScript adapters/database owners through all 436,555 Jitendex rows: outputs, plans, counters, and authoritative bytes match before and after publication.

The compiled scanner shrinks from 1,624 to 1,587 bytes. These results establish reduced writes and identical results; they do not establish whole-import latency or peak-memory gains.

Report, source identities, exact runners, raw receipts, and qualification limits: [dev/perf/canonical-journal-20261123/README.md](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/8282d596809d76ca2960f926719d94877925489e/dev/perf/canonical-journal-20261123/README.md).

## Validation

- Passed: 87 focused tests in seven files, including collision, rollback, trap, exact-candidate boundary, and old-ABI coverage.
- Passed: all four TypeScript projects, scoped JavaScript/JSON lint, and Markdown formatting.
- Passed: pinned Clang/LLD 21.1.8 WASM reproducibility and all seven target dry builds.
- Independent review verified implementation invariants and proof hashes.
- The local full-unit attempt was interrupted without a summary and is explicitly recorded as incomplete. Browser execution is unavailable in the local environment. Normal full-unit and browser CI checks remain required; this PR is a draft while they run.

## Contribution licensing and provenance

Changes are derived from this repository's existing GPL-3.0-or-later implementation. No new external implementation code or dependencies. The ABI 1 compatibility fixture is the existing checked module from the pinned baseline. This owner-authored, same-repository PR uses the paperwork exemption documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.

open.title: Encode repeated record fields in runs on direct output columns
open.head: bb1073961bb5adaa190e32943c94d063a18aa8bd
open.body:
## Problem

Resolved record fields repeat across adjacent dictionary rows, especially VNDB aliases. The encoder still validates and writes repeated content spans and interns repeated scores separately.

## Change and dependency

Plan content references and scores in independent runs for the existing private, factory-created typed-column path. Validate each consecutive content reference once, intern each consecutive score run once, and fill longer runs directly into final output columns.

This PR is **stacked on #849**, at `10a8f09e96ff943ec1351b1391cb56fa7e20feed`. It preserves direct final offset/length columns and does not restore their temporary allocation or copy. Retarget only after the parent is integrated.

Keep the existing origin/shape guard, first-occurrence score order, stored formats, length/offset validation, and generic, Float64, fixed-span, shared, accessor, proxy, and subclass fallbacks. Content and score runs remain independent because aliases may share content while carrying different scores.

## Result: retain as draft

All three [complete-dictionary six-block screens](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45265448894) passed correctness, but **none establishes a whole-import speedup**.

| Dictionary | Candidate B / parent A, paired median | Candidate B / identical parent C | Identical control C/A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict | +2.225% | −0.978% | +2.753% |
| Jitendex | +0.125% | −1.482% | +1.190% |
| VNDB | −0.812% | −0.549% | +0.152% |

Every candidate interval crosses zero. All six planned blocks and both separate exhaustive-media diagnostics per dictionary are retained, including large first-block control drift. No dictionaries or cohorts are pooled. The source structure suggests fewer repeated operations on VNDB, but the measured complete-import results remain inconclusive.

## Validation

- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45265381619): all 15 executed jobs passed; four conditional jobs skipped. Full unit, build, four TypeScript projects, JavaScript lint, Chromium/Firefox E2E, and the Anki matrix are green.
- 272 focused tests passed across seven suites.
- Independent differential review covered 196 cases: 99 legacy outputs, 57 compact outputs, and 40 matching errors.
- Complete locked-source replay: **7,613,164 rows / 937 banks**, byte-identical record fields versus the exact parent in two span layouts: constant 20-byte spans and actual native token lengths, including deterministic offsets above 1 TiB.
- The replay covers 528,299 JMdict rows, 436,555 Jitendex rows, and 6,648,310 VNDB rows. It validates record-field bytes, not whole-database semantic equality.
- All 60 browser observations passed inventory/restart checks, 72 sampled lookup receipts per observation, and equal storage sizes. Separate diagnostics read every referenced image: 236 Jitendex files and 146,570 VNDB files.
- Independent artifact audits verified exact source/tree/harness identities, package-entry receipts, raw browser-clock statistics, and correctness receipts.
- Earlier assertion timeout, killed lint, and explicitly constrained typecheck heap exhaustion are retained with the successful retries; exact-head hosted CI is green.

[Complete preserved evidence](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a4b7ba86fcffe90f9bfcd11d11999fae80c9b26f/docs/performance/import-crossover-20261123/REPORT.md) retains all original artifacts, scripts, byte oracles, source identities, CI receipts, and unsuccessful attempts alongside successful recoveries.

The separate low-level score-count correctness fix is #859; it is not included in this frozen performance source.

## Concurrent alternative

This is an alternative to #854, which batches joint content-and-score runs under the compact-metadata gate and retains staged columns. This PR uses independent runs and #849's direct final columns. Their encoder changes overlap; do not merge both implementations together.

Published tree `de8f9ef7ba011def59396fe64855fe22bebedac9` exactly matches reviewed local commit `22f09dd819b2e338f2e16daea9ef061fe1176878`.

## Provenance

Original changes to the repository's GPL-3.0-or-later implementation. No added dependency or third-party implementation. The existing same-repository owner acknowledgement exception applies.

open.title: perf: batch repeated content and score fields during imports
open.head: cda01e1ad1a29c8b4a6ad47e726c68152b478918
open.body:
## Problem

VNDB character rows frequently repeat both their resolved definition and score. Record-field encoding currently resolves the same content span and score-table entry for every row in those runs. The first pinned VNDB bank alone has 9,800 adjacent repeated-content-and-score rows out of 9,999.

## Change

For the existing parser-produced compact-metadata layout, encode equal content-reference/score runs with typed-array fills. Eligibility requires the existing factory-origin proof plus stable private reference and Int32 score columns. The ordinary scalar loop is retained for other inputs.

The first row of each run still performs normal reference validation and score interning. Run boundaries preserve first-use score order. Fixed-width, float64, shared, accessor-backed, external and malformed inputs retain their existing validation/fallback behavior. The persisted bytes and format are unchanged.

## Validation

- 246 focused tests across four suites passed.
- Main and test TypeScript and scoped ESLint passed.
- Two independent source reviews found no correctness blocker.
- A regression witness follows actual native compact metadata through worker-owned conversion, structured cloning, the production database factory and public record-store append, proving the optimized path is reachable.
- Byte-oracle tests cover score changes, content-run boundaries, large offsets, sentinel/legacy fallbacks and mutable/external input guards.

The full unit gate passed on the frozen product tree: **14,429 tests across 642 suites**, with 47 skipped, plus all **32 options tests**. The [complete source CI suite](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45263947741) passed all 15 normal jobs, including build/pinned WASM, all type/lint gates, Chromium and Firefox E2E, and the Anki matrix; four conditional jobs were skipped. The earlier interrupted local run is retained as incomplete; it is not counted as a pass.

The final field-byte oracle matched the baseline for **all 7,613,164 rows / 937 banks**. VNDB's field-encoding step was faster in all four fixed balanced pairs: −56.56% median paired change, −54.06% equal-work change, with 5,514,978 repeated scalar resolutions avoided in that component workload. Its explicit five-worker partition and synthetic offsets above 4 GiB differ from the current three-worker browser workload, so these counts and percentages are not claims about observed full-browser work. Both generic-path component controls retain their noisy tails.

All three complete-import cells are complete and inconclusive; their paired changes are within identical-product control drift. **Draft / HOLD: no complete-import speedup is claimed.** An earlier exploratory variant showed an ordinary-path overhead; this version restores the original scalar loop and requires the existing compact-metadata marker. Timing from that earlier variant is not evidence for this revision.

## Source identity

Parent: `3d65e403c644b9a5a6be3128d72f9d30050b70e0`.
Measured runtime commit `d2ab3344a483af52ac6d0765f3fbeaf8d1e2a0ca`, tree `24e3e31fb86f8c2587f1753f940da359162427cf`, exactly matches locally validated commit `e949286b9e5f37f98c2a400ee067928382c7b1f9`.
Documentation follow-up `cda01e1ad1a29c8b4a6ad47e726c68152b478918` changes only the existing performance handoff; all measured runtime, test and WASM blobs remain identical. Prettier and diff checks passed for the handoff.

## Provenance

Adapts the repository's existing GPL-3.0-or-later record encoder and test helpers. No third-party implementation was imported.

## Related work and complete-import study

[The frozen three-dictionary comparison](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45264553669) tests this exact product tree against two identical parent controls, with six balanced A/B/C blocks per dictionary and separate exhaustive media checks. All three cells completed successfully; final results are below.

Concurrent PR #849 changes the same record-field method to avoid temporary offset/length arrays. This PR instead reduces repeated content resolution and score interning within equal runs. At the reviewed #849 revision `10a8f09e96ff943ec1351b1391cb56fa7e20feed`, its direct path makes temporary offset/length columns null while this PR's run path fills those columns. The changes require deliberate integration and fresh validation; neither proposal is included in the other's measurements.

## Complete-import results — HOLD

| Dictionary | B/A paired median | B/C paired median | Identical C/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict | +1.813% | +2.235% | +2.860% |
| Jitendex | −1.190% | +0.490% | −0.878% |
| VNDB | −0.690% | −0.353% | −2.964% |

Positive means slower. Each cell retained all six balanced A/B/C blocks, three excluded warmups and two separate exhaustive diagnostics. All 69 observations passed source/package/fixture checks, restart/inventory, sampled content and lookup receipts, media checks and logical storage totals. VNDB's descriptive B/A interval is −6.495% to +2.735%; B/C is −2.150% to +4.011%. It was faster in three of six pairs against each baseline. The controls do not support a material total-import gain or negligible overhead claim.

The actual VNDB browser workload has three workers and 170 compact-metadata groups. Its data size produces the same 170 source groups as the component capture, but final ownership/score/slice admission is not instrumented; 170 compact groups must not be called 170 optimized chunks. Separate diagnostic field-encoding times were 287.5 ms for A and 145.5 ms for B. Those excluded diagnostics explain the mechanism and do not replace total-import results. No process-memory saving or exhaustive persisted lexical-byte equality is claimed.

**Keep this PR draft / on hold.** The complete observed cohort is retained; no selective timing rerun was made.

## Reproduction and retained evidence

The [single performance handoff](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/cda01e1ad1a29c8b4a6ad47e726c68152b478918/dev/perf/import-experiments-20260914.md) contains exact source/toolchain identities, reproduction commands, complete comparisons, independent reviews, scope limits, rejected JMdict attempts and remaining qualification. The [immutable evidence tree](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/d03649834ff5adc4fe484ea66b99cfe61c1eeed5/builds/perf/import-20261123-3aac) preserves all aggregate observations, package/fixture manifests, verification receipts, executed helpers and failed/incomplete local runs.

open.title: Compact projected media rows before worker transfer
open.head: 3597a103b0f35d076587e08196caa9f5d12f53ef
open.body:
## Problem

Once a parser worker has projected image paths, the importer only needs expression and reading diagnostics from the compatibility row. The worker nevertheless spreads the complete parsed row into the message, serializing unused presentation fields, hashes, numeric fields and empty content views for each projected image.

## Change

Represent projected media rows with four diagnostic fields: expression, reading, and their optional UTF-8 views. Keep the complete row for media that cannot use the projected-path fast path.

Use a discriminated row type throughout worker transfer collection and importer consumption. Persisted term columns, content slabs, image-path order, owned diagnostic views and fallback behavior are preserved. The importer rejects an impossible missing-diagnostics state before trying to interpret a compact row as a full row.

## Validation

- Exact published tree matches reviewed local commit `797f1a78fab8efde8ee7aff46369bd2d19a222f9`.
- 351 focused parser, importer and real-worker tests pass.
- Main and test TypeScript, changed-file ESLint and diff checks pass.
- Tests cover mixed compact/full rows, unsupported-media diagnostics, Unicode keys, single transfer of the owned key arena, and retained bytes after the worker handles another request.
- Independent source review completed.
- Complete source-copy replay: **7,613,164 rows / 937 banks**, with every remaining column, content buffer, key plan, prepared index, diagnostic key and projected path preserved. All **146,570 unique VNDB image paths** remain present.
- The fixed four-bank VNDB replay removes **1,760,664 row properties** (16 to 4 fields per projected row, 75%). Node V8 serialized media size falls from **56,685,599 B to 21,817,716 B**. This is scoped representation evidence, not Chrome wire size, peak memory or import time.
- [Reproducible component evidence](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/f18be706f665ba1228654452f38cef3a252a0aa8/docs/development/import-allocation-20261123/projected-media) records exact source/runner/archive hashes, fixed grouping, explicit parser settings, and the shared semantic path collector.
- All seven extension targets pass the local build dry run. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45262095863) and [frozen six-cell browser screen](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45262185499) are in progress; completed build and Chromium restart/interruption gates pass.

This remains a draft while verification completes. No complete-import speedup or peak-memory reduction is claimed. The fixed hosted screen compares this source separately against `3d65e403c644b9a5a6be3128d72f9d30050b70e0` on JMdict, Jitendex and VNDB with an identical-baseline control, restart checks and full persisted-media diagnostics.

This is independent of #845's decoding-scratch reuse; the two changes touch the same copying function but remove different work.

Original changes to existing GPL-covered code; no new dependencies or third-party implementation.

open.title: perf: avoid repeated dispatch for structured glossary strings
open.head: 09dfb90d926758205ff52d127ef3d950f0b15a65
open.body:
## Problem

Structured dictionary glossaries repeatedly return to the general JSON dispatch loop after validating an object key and consuming its colon, even when the next token is already known to be a quoted string. The pinned Jitendex archive contains 6,137,713 string-valued `content` fields.

## Change

Route that bounded quoted-value case directly through the existing string validation and object-value handling. Required fields, duplicate-key semantics, escapes, media hints, normalization hints, nesting limits and independent bank boundaries still use the established code.

This is a small control-flow change with no new allocation, cache, concurrency setting or persisted format. Regenerated source-bound WASM uses the repository's pinned Clang/LLD 21.1.8; the parser artifact grows by 37 bytes.

## Validation

- 1,365 focused parser tests across seven suites passed.
- Test TypeScript and scoped ESLint passed.
- Source CI passed 14,402 tests across 641 suites (47 intentionally skipped). A duplicate local run under concurrent test load had two 5-second timeouts in existing `term-entry-content-hash` cases; no assertion mismatch was reported. That failure is retained, and the exact-tree CI full unit/build passes are the authoritative gates.
- Independent source review found no correctness defect.
- Four alternating complete-Jitendex component pairs checked all 436,555 rows. Canonical content, key plans and every prepared index byte matched the parent in all observations; maximum WASM heap remained 89,063,424 bytes.
- The component candidate was faster in all four pairs, but absolute timing varied widely (parent 2.124–5.292 seconds, candidate 1.232–2.535 seconds). This is exploratory parser/lookup evidence, excluding worker transport, compression, OPFS and UI; it does not establish a complete-import speedup.

The [complete source CI suite](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45261383648) passed at this exact source revision: full unit/options tests, all TypeScript and lint gates, pinned WASM/build validation, Chromium and Firefox extension E2E, and the Anki matrix. Full-import assessment is complete. This PR stays draft because a material import benefit was not demonstrated.

## Source identity

Parent: `3d65e403c644b9a5a6be3128d72f9d30050b70e0`.
Published tree `1f9015b2176056ce75c26b5e02054fcd1fd673be` exactly matches locally tested commit `38e5d6dbda2bf1e2a809f32cc382ab16bac9ad47`.

## Provenance

Adapts this repository's existing GPL-3.0-or-later parser and tests. No third-party implementation was introduced.

## Complete-import screening update

The first frozen full-import screen is complete for JMdict, Jitendex and VNDB. Each uses six balanced A/B/C blocks (18 timed fresh-profile imports), three excluded warmups, and two separate exhaustive media diagnostics. A and C use exactly the same baseline package. Every completed run passed restart, persisted inventory, source-media and lookup-receipt checks.

| Dictionary | B/A paired median | B/C paired median | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| JMdict | +0.173% | +0.686% | Within baseline variation; no speedup established |
| Jitendex | +2.550% | +2.971% | No complete-import benefit; possible regression requires independent assessment |
| VNDB | +0.362% | −3.068% | Identical baseline C/A drift is +3.055%; inconclusive |

Jitendex's identical-code control varied from −9.34% to +20.71%, so the large local component gain is not an end-to-end result. All slow observations remain included. **Draft / do not promote:** the completed independent assessment below did not demonstrate a material benefit. All three dictionary screens finished successfully, including exhaustive equality of all 146,570 VNDB images (188,131,284 bytes) and identical persisted storage size (609,553,611 bytes).

[Raw screening workflow and retained artifacts](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45261611887). open.title: Overlap private content packing with compression workers

## Status

**Held in draft; not recommended for merge on the current evidence.** Correctness checks pass, but the complete-import results do not establish a reliable overall benefit. No process-memory improvement is claimed.

## Problem and change

Private dictionary content is packed into every compression block in a batch before any block is dispatched to a worker. This delays overlap between packing and compression and retains all packed input until dispatch.

Pack and transfer each private block as a compression worker finishes its preceding block. A batch keeps at most one active private input per worker, with ordered output. Concurrent batches have independent budgets; this is not a global or hard byte limit. Existing block plans, span coalescing, compression settings, dictionary bytes and stored layout are preserved. Producer/worker failures drain sibling work before the caller repacks stable source for its synchronous fallback.

The normal JMdict shared-content path remains unchanged. Large projected sources such as the locked Jitendex corpus use the private producer. This is separate from shared-source candidates #810/#839.

Do not promote this candidate. The frozen shared-content memory screen failed on Jitendex. In replication 2, all four observations met coverage rules, but median paired sampled maximum process-tree PSS increased **9.555%** and private bytes **11.517%**; both exceed the predeclared 5% median limit, and both private-byte pairs exceed the 10% individual limit. One hidden workflow source file omitted by artifact upload is supplied from the exact frozen Git tree, with its matching SHA-256 recorded separately and the original ZIP unchanged.

## Problem

Owned parser output is copied into private packing buffers before compression, even when compression workers can gather the same immutable bytes directly. The current Jitendex diagnostic attributes about 197 ms to content packing in a 1,383 ms complete import; this is a bottleneck observation, not a candidate speed estimate.

- Publish a fresh owned shared slab when the existing ownership rules admit it.

- Clear a compression message's source and span references only after its bytes have been successfully gathered into WASM.
- Preserve error ordering, source-consumed acknowledgement, block layout and compression settings.

This integration includes the currently merged strict parser, CRC reuse, source-read coalescing, content metadata publication and index I/O improvements. It does not alter either original PR branch.

## Problem

The parallel importer limits how many source groups workers can lead the ordered storage sink, but it does not use the retained owned-content byte count to restrict admission. A group backlog can therefore retain substantially more content than the active workers need.

open.title: Bound parallel parser lead by owned content bytes
open.head: c763a4c8e628e1cd0417102dfbddcc70b6440735
open.body:
## Problem

Parallel import workers are currently admitted by group distance. Owned-content bytes are recorded for diagnostics but do not restrict admission, so workers can build a backlog of content slabs while the ordered storage sink is busy. This is relevant to the memory increase measured for the shared-source path in #810.

## Change

Reserve each admitted group's known uncompressed source estimate. When parsing finishes, atomically replace that reservation with the exact owned backing-buffer size and hold it until the ordered sink settles.

The fixed budget is the existing 24 MiB group target multiplied by the unchanged worker count. Groups enter in source order. One oversized group can progress when the charged pipeline is empty. Output that exceeds its estimate blocks further admission; already admitted work can still exceed the budget.

Existing group-count admission, source grouping, ZIP prefetch, worker counts, compression reservations and ordered persistence remain unchanged. This accounting excludes prefetched ZIP buffers, retained WASM heaps, compression buffers and downstream storage, and is not an RSS ceiling.

open.title: perf: avoid copying immutable parser slabs into the term cache
open.head: 6b5e9af1edd1faabdc702fbd53e5dee81d5679d7
open.body:
## Problem and change

The recent-source deduplication cache copies an immutable parser slab when the retained content occupies only part of it. Trimming unused edges therefore adds a copy even when the importer already owns the complete backing buffer.

Allow the cache to retain a subrange view after consuming the existing one-time ownership witness. Charge the **entire backing allocation** against the cache budget, preserve FIFO eviction and rollback accounting, and copy the retained range when the backing allocation is too large or ownership is unavailable. Exact content comparisons still decide deduplication.

## Measured result and limits

On the pinned full JMdict archive, each candidate import adopts 101,143,281 cumulative payload bytes versus 76,482,945 for either baseline: **24,660,336 copied bytes avoided**. Cumulative retained payload bytes and the 3,998 recent-source hits match both controls in this fixture.

The independent 12-block study does **not establish a standalone total-import improvement against both controls**. A and C are identical baseline packages; B is this PR.

| Complete-import comparison | Paired median change | Descriptive 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| B/A | −0.697% | [−2.064%, −0.170%] |
| B/C | −1.387% | [−2.856%, +0.064%] |

Six-block Jitendex and VNDB screens likewise do not establish total-import gains. Charging unused backing bytes can reduce cache coverage on other inputs; the bounded budget remains enforced.

In the separate frozen 12-block VNDB qualification, the combined four-PR candidate's paired-median complete-import reductions were 3.5214% against A and 4.69394% against C. That result belongs to the combination and does not attribute a speedup to this cache change. JMdict/Jitendex total-latency gains remain unproven. See the [frozen evidence and retained observations](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a68ffd9596d03b9c922d5198c532ecb8e3706fea/docs/performance/import-runtime-20261123/README.md).

open.title: perf: reuse owned native lookup key buffers
open.head: 8fe5926cec1396a05ed4ea52be751e48784329b7
open.body:
## Problem

Native whole-chunk lookup indexes already contain an owned UTF-8 key arena and key-length table. The parser result copies both again into its key plan before transfer, adding work and another backing allocation.

## Change

When the native producer owns the complete sidecar and row byte lists are omitted, let its key plan refer to those exact owned subviews. A private WeakMap witnesses the producer and descriptor identities. Replaced descriptors fall back to ordinary copying; in-place edits stay visible to the current validation path. Explicit row-byte-list callers keep their existing aliases and copying behavior. Segmented and arbitrary split plans retain their existing contracts.

Retained record caches detach one tightly sized key arena when keeping a subview would otherwise pin the whole prepared sidecar. Normal OPFS imports discard these materialized records and keep the copy reduction. No grouping, concurrency, compression, or persisted format changes.

## Correctness and work reduction

- Complete stable row/content/media/key-plan/index outputs match baseline for all 526,942 JMdict, 435,448 Jitendex and 6,648,310 VNDB rows.
- Summed duplicate copied bytes removed in the serial corpus partitions: **8,301,780 JMdict; 9,706,463 Jitendex; 202,591,586 VNDB**. These are copy/allocation-volume reductions, not peak-memory or elapsed-time claims. Partitions have production-shaped group counts; exact bank membership was not independently matched to the browser planner.
- 234 parser/boundary and 195 record-store tests passed. Ownership coverage includes detached/transferred buffers, source reuse, descriptor replacement, in-place edits, explicit byte lists and retained-cache backing-buffer size/mutation independence.
- Main types, scoped lint and all-target build dry runs passed. The local complete test-type process was killed with exit 137 and no diagnostics; that original failure remains retained. [Hosted full CI 45122913657 passed](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45122913657), including the complete test-type gate, unit suites, pinned build, and Chromium/Firefox extension E2E. Optional workflow lanes were skipped, not represented as passes.
- Native WASM is unchanged.

## Performance decision: HOLD

Keep draft. The completed timing campaign does not establish a repeatable material complete-import gain. Four independent memory cells support small descriptive sampled-memory reductions; both JMdict memory cells remain unqualified. No all-corpus memory qualification or exact browser peak-memory claim is made.

### Complete-browser timing

[Run 45123053286](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45123053286) completed all six cells and **252 fresh-profile imports**: six excluded warmups, twelve adjacent alternating candidate/parent pairs and six interleaved same-code C/A pairs per cell, with independent reversed-order replication. Timing used Node 22.22.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12, identical production defaults and OPFS storage through the post-UI import-complete event. Twelve source-derived persisted probes and restart verification passed for every import.

Entries are **forward / reverse**; negative is faster. Equal work compares summed paired durations within one cell. No hosts are pooled and no control effects are subtracted.

| Dictionary | B/A median, F / R | B/A equal work, F / R | C/A median, F / R | C/A equal work, F / R |

open.title: Share owned dictionary content with compression workers
open.head: 5754e7837a6cea28debfd5d37a95c380d9bd4871
open.body:
## Review status

**Draft: measured time/memory tradeoff.** Jitendex imports are faster, but the separate full-process-tree study finds higher sampled memory usage. This candidate remains in draft for review of that tradeoff. The complete observations and a focused source-lifetime review are published below.

## Problem and change

Large projected dictionary imports already copy content into an independently owned buffer so parser workers can continue while the ordered sink finishes. Those private buffers force another main-thread packing copy before compression.

This change creates an independently owned SharedArrayBuffer for that content when shared buffers are available. Compression workers can use the existing shared-span path. The parser heap is still copied exactly once and can be reused immediately; published owned content remains immutable. Queue byte accounting and ownership witnesses remain in place, and the private-buffer fallback is preserved.

This PR is stacked on #801.

## Validation and timing

- 302 tests passed across parser, real worker transport, ownership and content-block storage suites. The tests mutate the original shared heap and reuse the real parser worker with different glosses, verifying that previously published content stays unchanged.
- The follow-up updates two existing ownership assertions to expect an independently owned shared buffer when available; that 146-test import-experiment suite passed. No runtime file changed after the measured candidate.
- Scoped lint and all current normal CI checks passed. [CI run](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45110941136).
- Final Jitendex qualification passed two independent, predetermined eight-pair AB/BA replications. Their median paired changes were **−14.94% and −14.52%**; the combined median of all 16 pairwise changes was **−14.56%, with 16/16 pairs faster**. Four A/A control pairs per replication were retained, spanning −7.01% to +0.92%. [Final campaign](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45113545482).
- The complete public lookup responses for all 12 deterministic source-derived terms match before/after restart, across arms and across replications. Every requested term is nonempty with no degraded dictionary availability. These are sampled semantic checks, not exhaustive all-term browser readback.
- The corrective all-corpus campaign also passed JMdict and VNDB. Their paired medians across 16 pairs were **−0.60% and +1.18%**, respectively, within broad control variation. No consistent timing benefit for those corpora is claimed.
- The frozen combination with #809 and #811 passed 782 focused tests, the all-target build check and all six browser replications. [Combined campaign](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45114362649).

## Physical layout and retained failures

Jitendex uses the existing JMdict compression dictionary. Shared owned content also qualifies for the existing initial reservation path, which writes the reference prefix before compressed blocks. Physical reference offsets therefore differ from the privately packed path.

The original comparison hashed physical offsets and raw reference previews and failed its cross-arm guard. A subsequent guard also flagged a counter derived from those previews. Both failed campaigns and every observation are retained separately.

The final harness preserves stable physical results within each package and across restart, independently recomputes every preview counter, and requires complete sampled semantic equality across packages. Independent audit found exactly 12 reference-offset changes, 12 raw-preview changes and one correctly derived preview-count change; every other physical field matched. A separate real-codec witness also matched all 4,534 distinct content spans from 5,448 rows in three pinned Jitendex banks (1, 110 and 218), plus complete compressed blocks, after source overwrite and cache invalidation.

## Memory qualification and decision

The separate [final process-tree memory campaign](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45116158450) used a frozen observer and four predetermined ABBA/BAAB imports in each of six jobs. All 24 imports preserve complete sampled public results across restart; 22 memory observations qualify.

- **Jitendex:** all four qualified pairs increase sampled maximum PSS by **8.16% to 11.11%**, with median paired increase **10.33%** (median absolute increase 134,125 KiB). Sampled private memory increases **10.15% to 13.81%**, median **12.84%**.
- **VNDB:** sampled PSS changes range from **−0.54% to +5.67%**, with three of four pairs higher and median **+4.60%**.
- **JMdict:** the qualified replication has PSS changes of **+1.56% and +2.58%**. Both baseline observations in the other replication remain unqualified because a zombie thread-group leader still has a live sibling thread; its maxima stay null and that job reports no pairs.

The observer records the full discovered renderer tree, stable process identities, every missing read and every narrowly verified exited-process exception. Both earlier memory campaigns and their failures remain unchanged. The window includes startup, import, semantic readback and browser restart. These non-atomic sampled maxima are not exact import-only peaks and do not establish memory nonregression.

The increase is material, so this PR remains a **draft**. A pinned source review found no explicit permanent source registry leak. Actual parser admission is bounded by group count; its owned-byte counter is diagnostic. Shared-buffer lifetimes and reservation overlap are possible explanations, but the measured cause remains unproven. No unmeasured cleanup or scheduling change is included in this PR.

## Reproducible evidence

[Component, ownership/layout and combined-test receipts](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/aa9e91660924fad0f3c918705f5c43b5c2d603ca/dev/perf/import-iteration-study-20261123/evidence/components/integration/README.md). [Final semantic/readback evidence](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/0d0c4fa7d1b073e0b4aaafa3d13b277a7b084a27/dev/perf/import-iteration-study-20261123/evidence/corrective-readback/README.md), [all combined observations](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/0d0c4fa7d1b073e0b4aaafa3d13b277a7b084a27/dev/perf/import-iteration-study-20261123/evidence/combined/README.md), [complete memory evidence](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/0d0c4fa7d1b073e0b4aaafa3d13b277a7b084a27/dev/perf/import-iteration-study-20261123/evidence/memory-zombies/README.md), [ownership/lifetime source review](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/0d0c4fa7d1b073e0b4aaafa3d13b277a7b084a27/dev/perf/import-iteration-study-20261123/evidence/ownership-lifetime-review.md), and the [evidence index](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/0d0c4fa7d1b073e0b4aaafa3d13b277a7b084a27/dev/perf/import-iteration-study-20261123/evidence/README.md) preserve original member bytes, source/package identities, failures, fixed pairs and standalone offline verifiers.

## Source and provenance

Current head: `5754e7837a6cea28debfd5d37a95c380d9bd4871`. Measured runtime: `51f095912b11ddd158ac173698eb322e2be99d12`; the follow-up changes only tests. Parent: #801 at `1e235059a4c05c2509e8757fccba43a2d60222df`.

Original changes to the repository's existing GPL-covered implementation; no new third-party implementation code.

open.title: Reduce redundant work in JMdict import and block reads
open.head: 1e82e1a237410c5a850661c1c361c444fa624546
open.body:
## Why

JMdict imports publish large ranges of content metadata one entry at a time and send compression workers hundreds of thousands of adjacent span descriptors. Persisted content reads also scan compressed payloads in JavaScript before copying them into the native decoder.

## Changes

- Validate consecutive reserved metadata ranges, bounds, hashes, states, and aliasing before publishing them with typed-array operations. Keep the original scalar fallback and its error behavior.
- Coalesce adjacent compression spans within the existing block plan. Preserve row references and full validation; cap staging and fall back on fragmented inputs.
- Verify both stored checksum words in the decoder's private native input allocation before decoding. Preserve generation checks, corruption precedence, output limits, and owned results.
- Retain the first pass's cached exact-match path, resolved record-field path, and proven final-cache-copy skip. The experimental early parser-lease release was reverted.
- Add a production-worker component harness, fixed four-arm controls, full persisted-artifact/source-row checks, and reproducible evidence.

Both arms of the final worker and production-reader comparisons include develop through `d733d0efe` and the first pass's changes. Those comparisons isolate this pass. The isolated publication replay was captured earlier in this pass, before that upstream merge.

## Measured evidence

| Change | Supported result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bulk metadata publication | About 26–33 ms saved; 86.67% / 86.90% paired method-time reduction in opposite orders | Isolated replay of all 360,859 publications; cache work excluded; duplicate controls retained |
| Coalesced compression metadata | 360,859 → 3,950 descriptors; 2,886,872 → 31,600 bytes in the two transport columns, **98.905% less** | Exact cumulative metadata work; 102 jobs and every compressed byte unchanged |
| Native checksum reader | Separate JavaScript payload traversal removed; real public-reader byte/corruption checks pass | Reverse timing favors it, but noisy forward controls prevent a replicated latency percentage |

The 96 timed production-worker observations plus eight warmups are **inconclusive for combined latency and CPU savings**. Identical-code arms varied substantially; the duplicate candidate in the reverse cohort was 3.42% slower by paired median. No whole-import speedup, peak-memory reduction, or browser latency percentage is claimed. All reports, controls, failures, and source identities are retained.

## Validation

- Full unit suite: **13,908 assertions passed, 47 skipped, across all 624 expected files**. Four sequential shards were reconciled against the complete inventory, with no missing or duplicate files.
- All four TypeScript projects and changed maintained JavaScript ESLint checks passed. Test fixture/mocking type errors were fixed; their failed and successful receipts remain in the archive.
- JMdict: all 526,942 reopened rows match source JSON; every stored byte matches control after validating and masking only paired random generation fields.
- JMnedict: the same proof covers all 667,942 rows through production workers.
- Jitendex: complete stored-artifact parity for 435,448 rows. No raw-source oracle is claimed because its media normalization mismatch also occurs on pristine baseline.
- JMdict with a 4 GiB hint: full sequential-component row/artifact parity, including 836 matches requiring persisted content. This does not reproduce the complete browser low-memory fallback.
- The actual production-reader study passed all 96 timed + 16 warmup full-byte comparisons and 44 corruption/generation checks.
- All-target build dry run and Chrome release builds passed. Four packaged JavaScript files and one source map changed versus the new control; all five WASM entries are byte-identical. The Chrome ZIP grows by 2,913 bytes; measured stored artifacts do not grow.

The [normal CI matrix](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/44826118534) passed on final head `1e82e1a237410c5a850661c1c361c444fa624546`, including Chromium and Firefox extension E2E. [Chromium restart/interruption recovery](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/44826118330) also passed. All eight triggered workflows are green. These correctness checks do not constitute a controlled import-performance comparison.

## Remaining gate

open.head: b9c9850a25eff3bb0684b8283cbb9b3c7ef49042
open.body:
## Summary

The fused dictionary parser validates keys and numeric tokens, then scans them again while interning keys and extracting int32 columns. This change retains the facts already established by the current row’s grammar scan.

- Carry per-row escape flags and bounded score/sequence values in a stack-local witness.
- Replace the per-digit division guard with an equivalent constant int32 boundary check.
- Preserve negative-zero scores, numeric fallback, malformed-input rejection, omitted/null sequences, metadata layout, exports, and persistent formats.
- Add 54 boundary, row-state, fallback, and recovery cases; rebuild pinned parser WASM with Clang/LLD 21.1.8.

The parser WASM grows by 235 bytes (52,930 → 53,165). The canonical scanner is unchanged. Worker counts, cache budgets, compression, source grouping, and import defaults are unchanged.

## Performance qualification — draft / hold

A complete-import speedup is not established. Two independent Linux cohorts each used twelve balanced baseline/candidate/identical-baseline triplets, two excluded warmup triplets, fresh profiles and OPFS stores, and exact source/package/fixture guards.

| Host | Candidate versus geometric controls, equal-work total | Identical-code C/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| EPYC 9V45 | -2.13% (95% paired interval -6.47% to +4.56%) | -1.03% |
| EPYC 9V74 | +1.65% (95% paired interval -1.18% to +4.42%) | +1.56% |

Every observation, including slower tails, is retained. Hosts are not pooled. Ordinary untraced reports show 10.97% and 4.92% lower summed elapsed native parse/encode/interning intervals; those overlapping worker intervals are neither CPU time nor total import time.

The first qualification run completed successfully: https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/44597837976

A separate previous-row key-reuse experiment is not included in this PR. Its incremental import results were mixed (-1.71% and +1.46%). A longer direct comparison of all combined changes against the original baseline completed 36 measured triplets per host: -1.38% (95% paired interval -3.10% to +0.40%) and -2.87% (-4.33% to -1.32%). The corrected unique-key native control showed +9.86% wall time / +20.64% process CPU on one host and -2.03% / -3.98% on the other. The key experiment remains separate and unqualified.

All 396 browser observations (360 measured, 36 warmups) are preserved. The original synthetic-control jobs failed in an untimed checker that assumed native lookup indexes; their completed browser results and partial native records remain retained. The corrected checker constructs missing indexes outside timing and preserves full-output parity requirements. No timings were discarded or rerun to select a favorable result.

[Complete investigation report](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/e3cdea3ea44d075127820aa28bf42fc8332888d6/dev/perf/import-experiments-20260914.md) · [Raw evidence and integrity index](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/e3cdea3ea44d075127820aa28bf42fc8332888d6/builds/perf/20261119-jmdict)

The evidence archive contains 1,656 original files, all six browser cohorts, both failed and corrected native controls, audits, prototype patches, and analysis scripts. Archive SHA-256: `d0bc67e55b553a18c6f1a2f22e5470f86f2ef21f166877ed828f334c1c63fdba`.

## Validation

[Core PR CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/44606333570), [static web acceptance](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/44606333606), CodeQL, actionlint, dependency review, and Chromium restart-interruption checks passed. All qualification jobs use Linux. The Firefox job permits existing unsupported-runtime skips, so its success does not establish complete Firefox functional coverage.

- Full Linux unit suite: 616 files passed; 13,720 tests passed, 47 skipped.
- Focused parser suites: 381 tests passed.
- Main, dev, test, and bench TypeScript checks pass after the test-only inference annotation in the current head. Runtime bytes match measured commit `45cc145f5273c100042b218eb4a0b5ce40bf5523`.
- All extension build targets pass; pinned WASM rebuild and packaged artifact checks pass.
- Complete row/content/key-plan/index-byte parity passes for JMdict (526,942 rows), JMnedict (667,942), and Jitendex (435,448). Native heap high-water marks and prepared-index sizes match baseline in those component checks.
- Release Chromium lifecycle passed 91 phases using the exact measured package, OPFS storage, zero import errors, and no skipped verification: update/concurrent lookup, restart persistence, batch import, hover/Reader flows, and deletion.

Whole-process memory, full persisted database equality, and cross-browser/device performance remain separate qualifications. This draft is for review of the tested implementation and evidence, not promotion of a claimed import speedup.

- [ ] I identified any copied, adapted, ported, translated, mechanically rewritten, or otherwise third-party-derived material and its license.

### Provenance notes

The changes adapt the repository’s existing GPL-3.0-or-later parser and test helpers. No third-party implementation was imported. The existing same-repository owner acknowledgement exception applies; no new licensing acknowledgement is asserted by this draft.
